Version status 2026-10: Sora 2 Pro is current; native audio sync; single generation can contain an internal cut
Use cases: Longer coherent clips / scene transitions / physics-driven motion
Syntax & camera movement: Write like a screenplay PARAGRAPH, not a comma-separated keyword string. 2-5 focused sentences. Order: camera & framing → subject & action → dialogue in quotes → audio direction → environment & lighting → style & mood. Sora defaults to FLAT lighting when unspecified — always state texture words (film grain, natural skin texture).
Temporal structure (start → mid → end): Describe cause→effect chains; Sora 2 handles physics better than any current model ("water splashes outward in slow motion as the bottle hits the floor"). A two-part scene with an internal cut works in one prompt.
Character consistency strategy: Anchor sentences at paragraph start; Sora supports character reference upload — attach once, reuse across clips
Exclusion / negative handling: Affirmative first. Never forget audio: omitting the audio layer wastes half the model's capability.

Version status 2026-10: Kling 3.0 family current; Omni adds multi-image anchoring; up to 6 shots per generation
Use cases: Short clips / character action / Chinese scenes / product physics
Syntax & camera movement: Four-part structure: 主体 + 动作 + 场景 + 风格(镜头/灯光/氛围). MUST include camera specs — omitting camera is Kling's #1 failure mode. Give motion verbs + timing markers ("在第2秒伸出手臂，随后转身"). Never stack more than two camera moves. Speaks Chinese and English; English usually more stable.
Temporal structure (start → mid → end): Beat-by-beat timeline across the duration. Multi-shot mode: label up to six shots in ONE generation to storyboard the sequence.
Character consistency strategy: Reference image locks identity; anchor sentences reused verbatim; Omni supports 3-8s clips with multi-image anchors
Exclusion / negative handling: Affirmative first; fallback 不要快速切换 / 不要换装 / 不要场景跳转

Version status 2026-10: Seedance 2.5 current; 30s native single-pass; up to 50 multimodal references; frame-accurate audio sync
Use cases: Long-form film-grade clips / brand TVC / causal narrative
Syntax & camera movement: Formula: 主体 + 动作 + 场景 + 镜头 + 灯光 + 风格 + 音效. Prefers LONG narrative prompts — describe the logic of the world, not just visual state ("蜡烛因为门被推开而摇曳"). Causal-chain writing is Seedance's strongest suit.
Temporal structure (start → mid → end): Native 30s single generation. Describe world logic and cause→effect rather than shot lists.
Character consistency strategy: Locked continuity tokens (face, product, colour, logo) carried across shots; consistent seed parameters
Exclusion / negative handling: Affirmative first; constraint items and output specs are both acceptable

Use cases: Precise controlled production / shot-accurate camera work
Syntax & camera movement: Most literal model — rewards concrete comma-separated technical descriptors. Long prompts up to 200 words parse cleanly. BEST when key params are lifted into NAMED FIELDS appended as a structured block: camera: 35mm, slow push-in / motion: ... / lighting: ... / style: ...
Temporal structure (start → mid → end): Explicit; Veo parses camera-left, foreground, background reliably. Dialogue-driven UGC: write the spoken line directly for lip-sync.
Character consistency strategy: Reference ingredients (subject, style frame, environment plate)
Exclusion / negative handling: Affirmative first; include audio cues inline ("the sound of liquid pouring into a glass")

Version status 2026-10: Gen-4.5 current; Gen-4 Turbo faster but less precise
Syntax & camera movement: SHORT and punchy — about 30 precise words beat 100 vague ones. Lead with the camera move and the action verb. Prompts past roughly 60-70 words are ignored; early tokens dominate. Gen-4 responds strongly to "anamorphic lens" / "shot on ARRI".
Temporal structure (start → mid → end): One primary action per clip; treat the model like talking to a DP ("now make the camera move slower").
Character consistency strategy: Reference-image-led phrasing — Gen-4 respects references well; use first-frame-as-anchor
Exclusion / negative handling: Affirmative first; keep it short or negations get dropped

Syntax & camera movement: Responds to STYLE keywords over physical description (stop-motion, claymation, flat illustration). Keep under 40 words — long descriptions lose coherence. Image-to-video with a clean packshot works best ("bottle rotates 45 degrees, label facing camera").
Character consistency strategy: Input image identity preserved; image-to-video is the consistency path

Version status 2026-10: Tops multi-image-to-video / image-to-video / video-edit categories; 15s max at 2K with native stereo
Syntax & camera movement: Lens-instruction writing style — write shots as lens commands. Multi-image-to-video is its strongest category.

Camera movement must be single-direction per clip; two conflicting moves waste credits and drift. EVERY movement must be paired with a speed (slow / deliberate / fast / creeping) — a naked move defaults to generic mid-speed.
Temporal structure (start → mid → end): Describe MOTION, never a static scene — a static description yields a still image with a subtle breathing effect. One primary motion only.
Character consistency strategy: Anchor sentences frozen for the entire clip; any mid-clip anchor edit is a P0 cross-frame break.
Exclusion / negative handling: Scene change / outfit change / camera direction change mid-clip = P0 failure
